_comment: Shared Go/TS golden for market settlement math (#0011 Decision 22). The Go settlement fold (backend/market) and the TS proceeds preview (frontend/lib) both assert against these exact cases, so the number a player is SHOWN can never silently diverge from the number that SETTLES. It is this capability's one remaining cross-language mirrored pair.

fold.name: fully covered by the top entry
fold._why: The ordinary case: one open request covers the whole sale, so nothing reaches the floor.

fold.name: split across a request and the floor
fold._why: The request runs out mid-sale and the remainder falls to the floor — the split that must be reported per portion, not blended into one number.

fold.name: split across two requests and the floor
fold._why: More than two entries, price-descending: proves the fold is one general rule rather than a two-case request/floor branch.

fold.name: floor only
fold._why: No open requests at all — the floor is the entry of last resort, not a fallback branch.

fold.name: per-portion rounding, not total rounding
fold._why: THE case that pins Decision 1's rounding granularity. Each portion floors separately: floor(10.5*140)=1470 and floor(9.5*100)=950, summing to 2420. Rounding the pre-summed fractional total instead would give floor(1470.0+950.0)=2420 here but diverges wherever the fractions compound — the two stacks must agree on which granularity they use.

fold.name: fractional portions each floor down
fold._why: Both portions carry a fraction that must be dropped: floor(3.33*7)=23 (23.31) and floor(6.67*3)=20 (20.01). Rounding the exact total (43.32) once would also give 43 here, but the per-portion loss is bounded per PORTION, which is the smaller, more conservative leak the milestone chose.

fold.name: a sub-ton sale that prices to zero
fold._why: Cargo is float64, so a fleet can hold a sub-ton fraction whose proceeds floor to zero. The fold reports 0 and the caller must REJECT the sale rather than debit cargo for nothing in return.

firstTonPrice.name: the top request sets the first-ton price
firstTonPrice._why: The slippage guard compares against this figure — the same one the price board showed the player moments earlier.

firstTonPrice.name: a nearly-drained request still sets it
firstTonPrice._why: THE case a first-ton-only guard fails on: one ton left at the premium keeps the guard passing while the rest of a large haul settles at the floor. This is why the optional minimum-total-proceeds guard exists beside it.
